evidence: All five dimensions use mode = "batched" (judge.toml line 3). Gates render and constraints use aggregation = "all_pass" (line 15) and are exempt. The three scored dimensions use weighted_mean (functional judge.toml:21, 43 criteria; polish :15, 5 criteria; visual :15, 5 Likert criteria). Each scored prompt has explicit independence and continue-after-failure wording: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own...'; polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' All scored prompts also say at line 7 'If a feature does not work as delivered, give that criterion its lowest score (binary 0; Likert 1), state what you observed, and move on', and the tool-limitation clause (functional:53, polish:18, visual:16) says 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' No scored prompt or criterion tells the judge to stop at the first failure (grep for stop/halt/abort/first fail found none in task scored prompts). The only blanket zero is the in-dimension browser gate (blank/static shell or failed shared-storage check), which the skill requires scored prompts to restate (deterministic-checks.md:52) and is not a first-criterion-failure stop. Cross-criterion references in functional/polish judge.toml (e.g. functional:65, 110, 236, 371, 380; polish:50) assign ownership to avoid double deduction rather than making one row's verdict depend on another. Wording is at least as strong as the template's ('Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'). Adversarial reasoning: a broken app that fails J1 setup cannot cascade zeros because the prompt mandates re-setup on a new job; a conforming app that fails one bulk-move row keeps other rows because sibling verdicts are declared non-evidence. Note (not a row-38 defect): polish hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (polish judge.toml:23, :32; weights 3+3 of 12) are each 0 if the live update never arrives, so a missing live-update transport also zeroes half of Polish; that is a precondition coupling within each criterion's own observable (row 28/40 territory), not a stop-on-failure instruction.
